title: Renewal Health Signals & Save Plays — working draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, ops-facing playbook for identifying at-risk contracts earlier via product and engagement signals, and for running lightweight 'save plays' that scale across mid-market and enterprise segments. Focus is on measurable triggers, short remediation experiments, and an exec-escalation cadence that respects customer signals and our capacity to intervene.

Status and intent:
- Draft: working template to standardize how CS and AMs triage and act on renewal risk.
- Goal: move high-signal at-risk customers into recovery (renewal retained) within a 90–120 day window before renewal date.
- Not a legal or pricing manual — coordinates with sales/legal on offers.

Core assumptions (working):
- We can surface product usage signals reliably via telemetry: active seats, daily active users (DAU) using LLM endpoints, average tokens/day per seat, error/latency anomalies.
- Engagement signals (QBR attendance, support volume, feature requests) correlate with churn risk.
- A tiered set of plays (light touch -> high-touch) improves ROI vs. ad-hoc escalation.

Health signals (primary) — compute weekly:
1) Usage falloff: >25% drop in MAU or tokens/week over 4 weeks vs. baseline.
2) Regression in latency/error: 2x increase in errors or sustained tail latency > SLA for >48 hrs.
3) Feature mismatch: customer has open product feedback >3 items unaddressed + NPS < 20.
4) Support volume spike: top-3 customers by ticket rate per seat increased >50% in 14 days.
5) QBR no-show: two consecutive missed QBRs or reschedules without agenda.

Secondary signals (contextual):
- Contract changes (headcount freeze, reorg mention in notes), renewal rep assignment missing, pre-billing disputes.

Signal scoring (example, WIP):
- Each primary signal = 2 points, secondary = 1 point. >=4 points => high-risk; 2-3 => medium; 0-1 => low. (Action table below keyed to score.)

Action matrix (score -> play cadence):
- Low (0-1): Auto-email nurture + health dashboard share. Owner: AM. Cadence: weekly automated check-ins.
- Medium (2-3): AM outreach + low-effort intervention (walkthrough, usage tips, quick performance review). Owner: AM + CS Ops. Cadence: biweekly.
- High (4+): Full Save Play (see below). Owner: named Customer Success Lead + Solutions Eng + Sales AE (if escalation needed). Cadence: weekly standups + exec touchpoints.

Save Play (high-risk) — template steps (editable):
1) Triage packet (24 hrs): compile: last 12 weeks usage, error/latency chart, support ticket summary, QBR notes, commercial terms & renewal date. Create single-page summary for exec.
2) Rapid remediation (48–72 hrs): apply quick wins: reconfigure routing to lower latency, increase burst capacity on Dedicated if cost-approved, patch model variant fallback if hallucinations/regressions. Document change and rollback plan.
3) Engagement blitz (7 days): schedule a targeted working session: Solutions Eng does 60–90 minute deep-dive; propose 3 prioritized requests with owners.
4) Temporary concession options (if required): 1-month credit, extended pilot for new feature, pilot access to Dedicated burst days. All concessions to be approved by Commercial Ops and Legal.
5) Exec escalation (if remediation not improving in 14 days): brief Head of CS => SVP Customer Success. Exec email template (example in appendix).
6) Renewal decision window (30 days before renewal): if improved -> standard renewal cadence; if not -> handoff to deals desk + commercial for structured renewal offer.

Escalation matrix (roles + cadence):
- Day 0: AM + CSM (owner) creates triage packet.
- Day 3: Solutions Eng assigned for remediation.
- Day 8: CS Manager reviews outcomes; if unresolved, escalate to Director of CS with proposed concession.
- Day 14: If still unresolved, SVP notified; prepare exec briefing slide (1 slide) and 15-minute sync with customer exec or internal exec as appropriate.

Practical playbook artifacts (checklist):
- [ ] Triage packet saved to customer folder and linked on Jira ticket.
- [ ] Telemetry snapshot (PDF/CSV) attached.
- [ ] Support owner assigned and SLA response logged.
- [ ] Working session scheduled with agenda + success criteria.
- [ ] Remediation actions documented with rollback steps.
- [ ] Concession proposal prepared (if needed) with approval path.
- [ ] Exec briefing drafted if >14 days unresolved.

QBR and renewal-ready template (short):
- One-page QBR slide components (to be included in QBR doc):
  * Executive summary: current health score and trend (green/amber/red).
  * Usage snapshot: tokens/week, DAU, top 3 flows.
  * Issues and actions: top 3 blockers and owners.
  * Opportunity: feature adoption or optimization with estimated value.
  * Ask: specific approvals needed before renewal.

Renewal tracker snippet (CSV-style lines we paste into shared sheet):
- Columns: customer_id, customer_name, renewal_date, cs_owner, risk_score, last_action, next_step, concession_requested, legal_needed
- Example row: R-001234, "Fathom Health", 2025-06-15, Aisha Patel, 5, "Remediation in progress", "Exec dive 2025-05-10", "1 month credit", "yes"

Customer-facing language (short save play email template):
Subject: Quick plan to stabilize performance ahead of renewal
Hi [CustomerFirstName],
We’ve been reviewing usage and saw a spike in errors and a drop in some key flows. We value your partnership and want to propose a 2-week remediation + working session with our engineering leads to resolve the root causes quickly. Can you join a 60-min session next week?
Thanks,
[CS Name]

Internal exec email (short):
Subject: Exec brief — at-risk renewal: [CustomerName] — action requested
Body: One-pager attached: health score, top blockers, remediation steps taken, requested concession and approval path. Recommend 15-min sync if no improvement in 5 business days.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Threshold tuning: initial thresholds are conservative; need to validate with historical renewal outcomes (ask Data Science to run a backtest).
- Automation: can we bake the score into the health dashboard and alert via Slack? (CS Ops + Platform).
- Legal/commercial guardrails for typical concessions by tier.
- Regional variation: APAC customers sometimes show seasonal usage patterns; consider zone-specific baselines.

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- Example triage packet template: /templates/triage-packet-v1.pptx (WIP)
- Example working session agenda (bullet list) attached in the customer folder.
- Past saved wins: link to case studies (internal) — saved-wins/2024-q3.md

Notes to self and small print (voice-of-doc):
- Keep plays short and measurable. Avoid unlimited discounts — prefer timeboxed pilots or credits.
- Emphasize reliability fixes before feature promises.
- This doc will be iterated after a 6-week pilot with 5 mid-market accounts.

End of draft.

(If you copy/paste into Google Doc, consider converting 'Save Play' steps into a checkable table for AMs.)
